title: Quantum reference activation of classical symmetric channels
abstract: We determine the complete equal-reference contraction coefficients of a classical symmetric channel with an arbitrary finite quantum reference. For an alphabet of size n and stochastic parameter -1/(n-1) <= lambda <= 1, the coefficients for the SLD metric, minimal chi-square divergence, triangular Petz divergence, BKM metric and Umegaki relative entropy equal (n-1)lambda^2/[1+(n-2)lambda]. A cyclic harmonic bound supplies the upper estimate and a separable classical-quantum simplex supplies matching faithful limits. The ordinary classical coefficient is n lambda^2/[2+(n-2)lambda]. Every restriction to two input symbols retains that ordinary coefficient even with a quantum reference, so classical binary-support reduction fails in the complete setting. At the exclusion endpoint, the complete coefficient is one although every two-symbol restriction has coefficient 1/(n-1). A family of actual binary measurements, controlled by the classical output, witnesses near-unit retention for a fixed three-symbol channel and a fixed three-dimensional reference. Input, quantum output and measured output relative entropies all tend to log 2. Conditioning grows exponentially and the useful probabilities become rare; no robust communication or capacity advantage is claimed. Adverse finite examples and review-context limitations are retained.
